gap: No result ChatGPT got states that VIA writes the keymap, layers and macros into the keyboard's own non-volatile memory over a USB link (four layers by default), or that the Lofree Flow 2 only appears in VIA after you plug it in by cable and load Lofree's JSON definition through VIA's Design tab.
standout_why: Compared against mechkeyfoundry.com (the cited best-of page and its three-way comparison) and mkbguide.com; rtings.com's best-of page returned only navigation, so its pick text was not compared. mechkeyfoundry has part of it: it says the K3 Max keymap 'is compiled onto the board and travels with it' and that the Flow 2 'supports VIA for remapping over 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5.3 or USB-C'. Neither page gives the setup path (cable, Design tab, JSON file), the layer count, or the VIA project's own wording on where the keymap is stored. mkbguide lists only 'VIA configuration' for the Flow 2 and 'NuPhyIO 2.0' for the Air75 V3. Caveat: lofree.co, keychron.com and nuphy.com all returned HTTP 429 today, so the Flow 2 specifics rest on VIA's docs plus one named third-party guide, not on Lofree's own page.
decides: It confirms the Lofree Flow 2 84 as a linkable pick for programmers who want layers and remaps that work on any OS with no background app, because VIA stores them on the board. It adds a caveat the page must state: setup is not plug-and-detect (cable plus a manually loaded JSON), which the Keychron K3 Max avoids according to mechkeyfoundry (remaps through Keychron Launcher in a browser). It also separates firmware-stored boards (Flow 2, K3 Max, K1 Max) from host-app boards: mechkeyfoundry says the MX Mechanical Mini remaps through Logi Options+ on Windows and macOS only, and mkbguide says the Flow Lite84 uses Lofree Key Mapper for Windows and Mac, so a Linux programmer should not pick those for remapping. The NuPhy Air75 V3 moved from QMK/VIA to NuPhyIO 2.0 (mkbguide), so the 'QMK/VIA preferred' line in ChatGPT's own table no longer describes its top pick.

findings.label: Where VIA keeps a remap
findings.value: VIA 'stores dynamic keymaps, macros, layout options, and other supported settings in the keyboard's non-volatile memory'
findings.note: VIA project's own documentation, quoted as the fetch tool returned it. Applies to any VIA-compatible board (Lofree Flow 2, Keychron K3 Max / K1 Max).

findings.label: How VIA reaches the keyboard
findings.value: 'VIA communicates with compatible firmware over USB'
findings.note: The page does not say whether a 2.4 GHz dongle (which is also a USB device) counts; it does not mention Bluetooth.

findings.label: Layers VIA provides by default
findings.value: 4 dynamic layers ('By default, VIA provides four dynamic layers'); the count is set by the firmware's dynamic_keymap.layer_count
findings.note: Default for VIA firmware in general; a maker can build with a different count.

findings.label: Connection needed to configure in VIA
findings.value: Wired: 'Flow2 needs to be connected to the PC by wire' (Flow2をパソコンに有線でつなげておく必要があります)
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow2 の VIA 設定方法!キーマップの変更方法について (ばんか / bamka, note.com)
findings.note: Named third-party guide by bamka, published 2025-09-08; translation by the fetch tool. Not Lofree's own wording. It sits in tension with mechkeyfoundry's 'supports VIA for remapping over 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5.3 or USB-C', which may only mean remaps keep working in those modes.

findings.label: VIA setup steps
findings.value: Download Lofree's 'Flow2 VIA Json' file, turn on 'Show Design tab' in VIA's settings, open Design and click Load to load the JSON
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow2 の VIA 設定方法!キーマップの変更方法について (ばんか / bamka, note.com)
findings.note: bamka, 2025-09-08. The guide names the file FLOW2-100key-OE928-Json-20250905.json for the unit it covers; the 84-key file name was not on this page. The guide took the download link from Lofree's Kickstarter page.

findings.label: Firmware internals (reverse-engineering note)
findings.value: 6-layer default keymap block in the firmware image; USB VID/PID 0x388D / 0x0001, same ID on the 2.4G dongle; firmware upgrade uses WB32 DFU through QMK Toolbox
findings.note: Third-party analysis by GitHub user seobaeksol, covering the OE928 (100-key) definition. Not a Lofree statement; use only as supporting colour, and do not print '6 layers' as a Lofree spec.

findings.label: WebHID availability (the browser API web configurators use)
findings.value: MDN: 'This feature is not Baseline because it does not work in some of the most widely-used browsers'; marked experimental
findings.note: The compatibility table did not load, so the list of supporting browsers is not sourced from this page (see unsourced).

findings.value: 'Keychron's K3 Max runs QMK and remaps through Keychron Launcher or VIA'; 'your keymap is compiled onto the board and travels with it'
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 vs Lofree Flow 2 vs Keychron K3 Max (mechkeyfoundry.com)
